intro: These profiles are brief reminders of courage, scholarship, and trust in Allah — not exhaustive biographies. For fiqh, follow qualified teachers in your school (madhhab) and local scholars.

figures.name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
figures.arabic: خَدِيجَةُ بِنْتُ خُوَيْلِدٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا
figures.summary: The first to believe; supported the Message with unwavering stability, wealth used in service of truth, and deep emotional refuge for the Prophet ﷺ in the hardest first years.
figures.lesson: Strength can look like quiet constancy: believing early, carrying cost, and staying kind.

figures.name: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
figures.arabic: عَائِشَةُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا
figures.summary: A scholar of the Ummah: fiqh, hadith, and seerah memory carrier; questions refined understanding; leadership of knowledge with adab.
figures.lesson: Seeking knowledge is worship when paired with humility and careful transmission.

figures.name: Umm Salamah Hind bint Abi Umayyah
figures.arabic: أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ هِنْدُ بِنْتُ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا
figures.summary: Hijrah trials, patience under separation and loss, and counsel remembered in seerah — a voice of measured wisdom in community decisions.
figures.lesson: Sabr is not silence only; it can be strategic trust while wounds still ache.

figures.name: Asma bint Abi Bakr
figures.arabic: أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا
figures.summary: Known for resourcefulness and courage in hardship; the 'Dhat an-Nitaqayn' story reflects loyalty and creative service in difficulty.
figures.lesson: Creative effort in obedience: using what you have to protect others.

fiqhNotes.title: Prayer, hayd, and nifas
fiqhNotes.body: Menstruation (hayd) and post-natal bleeding (nifas) pause salah and fasting as defined by classical fiqh; make up missed prayers differs from missed fasts of Ramadan — learn the details from a qualified teacher.

fiqhNotes.title: Dress and modesty
fiqhNotes.body: Aurah rules vary by context (prayer, Hajj zones, etc.). Take rulings from trustworthy scholarship rather than general articles alone.

fiqhNotes.title: Mosque attendance
fiqhNotes.body: Scholars differ on emphasis for women praying at home vs mosque; adab in either case includes not crowding harm, avoiding perfume for prayer in public rows where discouraged, and following local guidance.

fiqhNotes.title: Seeking knowledge
fiqhNotes.body: There is ijazah and adab in transmission — prioritize teachers who link fiqh to mercy and community responsibility.
